lessons_learned.lesson: Recursive waves discover that prior waves already solved many planned fixes
lessons_learned.evidence: Kilo found 6 of 8 planned P0 fixes already applied. Lima found filtering and batching already built. This is a feature, not a bug -- it validates prior work and frees capacity for new problems.
lessons_learned.implication: Future waves should plan verification tasks alongside implementation tasks, with fallback work if items are already fixed.

lessons_learned.lesson: Each wave naturally specializes: Wave 1 = build, Wave 2 = integrate, Wave 3 = harden
lessons_learned.evidence: Wave 1 created 13 new files (6657 lines). Wave 2 modified 88 existing files. Wave 3 created 10 new resilience modules and verified everything with benchmarks.
lessons_learned.implication: Plan wave missions around this natural build/integrate/harden progression.

lessons_learned.lesson: Quality verification teams (Epsilon, TEAM-J, Oscar) are essential for multi-wave programs
lessons_learned.evidence: Oscar's 16 integration tests and 6 benchmarks caught zero regressions and confirmed all targets met. This gives confidence that 3 waves of changes compose correctly.
lessons_learned.implication: Always include a dedicated quality/verification team in each wave.

lessons_learned.lesson: Status write deduplication delivered the single largest overhead reduction (99%)
lessons_learned.evidence: Kilo's simple cache-and-compare in update_status() reduced DB writes from 100 per 100 updates to 1, because most status updates are identical repetitions.
lessons_learned.implication: Profile before optimizing -- the biggest wins are often in the most mundane code paths.

lessons_learned.lesson: New resilience modules (circuit breaker, deadlock detector, etc.) must be actively wired in to deliver value
lessons_learned.evidence: Mike and November built 6 production-ready modules but they are not yet integrated into the coordinator heartbeat loop or multi_team_runner.
lessons_learned.implication: Wave 4 should prioritize wiring over building. The tools exist; they need activation.

lessons_learned.lesson: The 3-agent team size (lead + 2 devs) consistently works well across all 15 teams
lessons_learned.evidence: Every team across 3 waves completed their mission with 3 agents. No team reported needing more or fewer agents.
lessons_learned.implication: Standardize on 3-agent teams for future multi-wave programs.
